title: Maximum Trailing Zeros in a Cornered Path
summary: Given a 2D grid of positive integers, find the maximum number of trailing zeros in the product of any cornered path.
statement: Given a 2D grid of positive integers, find the maximum number of trailing zeros in the product of any cornered path. A cornered path can turn at most once, moving exclusively in one direction until the turn, then switching direction. The path cannot revisit any cell. Horizontal movement is left or right, and vertical is up or down.
constraints: A path moves horizontally and vertically, turns at most once, and never revisits a cell.
Its product trailing-zero count is min(total factors of two,total factors of five).
Return the maximum over straight paths, single cells, and all four corner orientations.
hints: Trailing zeros depend only on counts of prime factors two and five.
Build row and column prefix sums for both factor counts, then combine one horizontal arm with one vertical arm at each turn.
Subtract the pivot once because both inclusive arms contain it; score each orientation with min(twos,fives).
Every allowed corner chooses one of four arm pairs, and prefix sums give its exact factor totals, so taking their maximum covers all paths.
editorial: Every allowed corner chooses one of four arm pairs, and prefix sums give its exact factor totals, so taking their maximum covers all paths.

tests.explanation: An optimal corner product contains three matched factor pairs of two and five.
A path through all but one suitable corner can accumulate three trailing zeros.
